;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Nicaraguan protests]]
**Catholic bishops cancel the planned [[Episcopal Conference of Nicaragua|Episcopal Conference talks]] with the [[Government of Nicaragua|government]] after protests against [[Nicaragua]]n [[President of Nicaragua|President]] [[Daniel Ortega]] turn violent. According to the Nicaraguan Human Rights Center, pro-government armed groups killed 11 people. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nicaragua-protests/eleven-killed-in-nicaragua-protests-including-attack-on-mothers-day-march-idUSKCN1IW27E (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Transport in Iran]]
**Truck owners' strikes continue for the tenth consecutive day in 177 cities. Fuel shortages and long lines at petrol stations are reported in all major [[Iran]]ian cities. [https://www.opendemocracy.net/jubin-afshar/iran-truckers-join-nationwide-push-for-change (Open Democracy)]
*[[First Trump tariffs|Trump tariffs]], [[Protectionism in the United States]]
**[[United States]] tariffs of 25% on steel and 10% on aluminium imports from [[Canada]], [[Mexico]] and the [[European Union]] are set to take effect at midnight<!-- timezone? -->. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-44320221 (BBC)]
**Mexico retaliates with equivalent levies on [[Pig's trotters|pork legs]], apples, grapes, cheeses and steel. The [[Secretariat of Economy (Mexico)|Secretariat of Economy]] says that the measures will be in place until the U.S. eliminates their new tariffs. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-mexico/mexico-hits-back-at-u-s-steel-aluminum-tariffs-with-equivalent-measures-idUSKCN1IW1ZI (Reuters)]
**[[President of the European Commission]] [[Jean-Claude Juncker]] vows "counterbalancing measures" from the EU soon. The EU is expected to respond with tariffs on a little more than US$3 billion worth of American goods including motorcycles, [[Bourbon whiskey|bourbon]], and blue jeans. Juncker also says that the EU will proceed with a [[Dispute settlement in the World Trade Organization|case]] against the US in the [[World Trade Organization]]. [[United States Secretary of Commerce|US Secretary of Commerce]] [[Wilbur Ross]] replies that the EU measures are "unlikely" to have much impact on the US economy. [http://www.newsobserver.com/news/business/article212244199.html (AP via ''The News & Observer'')] [https://www.businessinsider.nl/trump-steel-aluminum-tariffs-trade-war-europe-canada-mexico-2018-5/ (''Business Insider'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-ross-retaliation/us-commerce-chief-any-reprisals-over-metals-tariffs-unlikely-to-hit-us-economy-idUSKCN1IW20F (Reuters)]
**[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Canada)|Canadian Foreign Minister]] [[Chrystia Freeland]] announces dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs of 10% or 25% on a list of goods – steel, aluminum, whiskey, orange juice and other food products – worth [[Canadian dollar|$]]16.6 billion. [[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] denounces an "affront" to the [[Canada–United States relations#Military and security|security partnership]] between the US and Canada. [https://www.cnbc.com/2018/05/31/canada-announces-retaliatory-tariffs.html (CNBC)]

;International relations
*[[Support for military action against Iran]]
**Ex-[[Israel]]i spy chief Tamir Pardo reveals that [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] had ordered the [[Israeli Defence Forces]] to prepare for military action against [[Iran]] in 2011. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/israeli-spy-chief-netanyahu-planned-iran-strike-2011-55553336 (ABC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[European Convention on Human Rights]]
**The [[European Court of Human Rights]] rules that the [[Romania]]n and [[Lithuania]]n governments each knowingly hosted [[CIA secret prisons]] around 2005. Both countries also participated in the US [[extraordinary rendition]] program: one case by each country is acknowledged. Four years ago, [[Poland]] was also condemned for running a [[Central Intelligence Agency|CIA]] secret jail. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-rights-cia-prisons/romania-and-lithuania-knowingly-hosted-secret-cia-jails-european-court-rules-idUSKCN1IW1PF (Reuters)]
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**A British man named Husnain Rashid pleaded guilty after supporting [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIS]] and admitting that he threatened to attack [[Prince George of Cambridge|Prince George]] at school. [https://globalnews.ca/news/4245398/prince-george-terrorism-attack-isis/ (Global News)]
*[[Denmark]]'s [[Folketing|parliament]] votes 75–30 to ban [[hijab by country|garments]] that cover the face, which includes [[Islam]]ic veils such as the [[niqāb]] and [[burqa]]. Those violating the law risk a fine of 1,000 [[Danish krone|kroner]]. Similar bans already exist in [[Austria]], [[Belgium]] and [[France]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/may/31/denmark-passes-law-banning-burqa-and-niqab (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2018 vote of no confidence in the government of Mariano Rajoy]], [[Gürtel case]]
**The debate on a [[motion of no confidence]] against [[Prime Minister of Spain|Spanish Prime Minister]] [[Mariano Rajoy]]'s government takes place at the [[Congress of Deputies]], with a vote scheduled tomorrow. With an expected 180 votes against 176 needed, leader of the Opposition, [[Spanish Socialist Workers' Party|socialist]] [[Pedro Sánchez]], could immediately become the next Prime Minister. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/spain-mariano-rajoy-no-confidence-vote-basque-catalan-corruption-a8377331.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-spain-politics/opposition-secures-enough-votes-to-topple-spains-rajoy-idUSKCN1IW0TM (Reuters)]
*[[Thirty-first Amendment to the Constitution of Pakistan]]
**[[Pakistan]]i [[President of Pakistan|President]] [[Mamnoon Hussain]] signs into law the official merger of the [[Federally Administered Tribal Areas]] with the [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]] administrative province. [https://www.rferl.org/a/pakistani-president-signs-law-merging-tribal-areas-with-khyber-pakhtunkhwa/29261314.html (RFE/RL)]
*A large march, which included students, citizen collectives and political groups of the left, toured the streets of Lima, Peru to demand the closure of the [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|Congress]] of the Republic, seat of the legislative power, in response to the constant corruption scandals involving congressmen, in addition to excessive economic expenses that, for the demonstrators, makes this power of the State. The protest, initially peaceful, turned violent when the police prevented the demonstrators from approaching precisely the Congress and the presidential palace. [https://peru21.pe/lima/desarrolla-marcha-denominada-cerremos-congreso-lima-video-408861?foto=10 (''Perú 21'')] [https://larepublica.pe/politica/1253191-marcha-congreso-gasolinazo-termino-enfrentamientos-fotos/6 (''La República'')]

;Science and technology
*[[Plutino]]s
**Astronomers announce the discovery of {{convert|380|-|680|km|adj=on}} wide [[plutino]] {{mpl|2017 OF|69}}, the fifth-largest known plutino, and the largest discovered since [[90482 Orcus]] in 2004. [https://minorplanetcenter.net/mpec/K18/K18KA9.html (Minor Planet Center)]
**[[Pluto]], the eponymous member of the [[plutino]] group, is discovered to have [[dunes]] of [[methane]] ice. [https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-44317367 (BBC)]
*[[Paleontology|Paleontologists]] at the [[University of Bristol]] announce, through the ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' journal, the discovery of the world's oldest lizard fossil, estimated to be 240 million years old. The fossil, ''[[Megachirella wachtleri]]'', is the most ancient known ancestor of all modern [[lizard]]s and [[snake]]s. [https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2018/05/180530142043.htm (''Science Daily'')] [http://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/megachirella-lizard-1.4682553 (CBC)]
